title: Neuroanatomy and functional systems
stage: College neuroscience and cognitive science degree
audience: a college student in a neuroscience, cognitive science, psychology or biology degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn the structure of the nervous system and how its parts work together: development and the plan of the nervous system, the spinal cord and brainstem, cranial nerves, the thalamus and hypothalamus, the cerebral cortex and its areas, the basal ganglia and cerebellum, the limbic system, blood supply and the ventricles, the major pathways for sensation and movement, and how the location of damage predicts what a person loses.
primary_reading: Neuroscience Online, an open-access textbook from McGovern Medical School at UTHealth Houston (free)

weeks.1: Development and the plan of the nervous system
weeks.2: Directions, planes and the meninges, ventricles and blood supply
weeks.3: The spinal cord and spinal reflexes
weeks.4: The brainstem and the cranial nerves
weeks.6: The cerebral cortex: lobes, areas and layers
weeks.8: Motor pathways and the corticospinal tract
weeks.9: The basal ganglia and the cerebellum
weeks.10: The limbic system, hippocampus and amygdala
weeks.12: Localizing lesions: from symptoms to sites

blocks.deliverable: Describe the brain in standard anatomical terms.
Trace a spinal reflex and test the cranial nerves in words.
Match cortical areas to their functions and inputs.
Week 7 midterm; trace the pathways for touch, pain and voluntary movement.
Explain the effects of damage to the basal ganglia and the cerebellum.
Localize the lesion in written clinical vignettes.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Pathway atlas: write a pathway atlas, in words and tables, of five major pathways (touch, pain, vision, hearing and voluntary movement), each traced from receptor or cortex to target with every relay and decussation, and use it to localize the lesions in six supplied vignettes.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
